name: Seagate Technology
window: Q3 FY26 print + intra-quarter · Apr 28 → Jul 28, 2026

events.text: Q3 FY26 (March quarter, beat-and-raise): revenue $3.1B (+44% YoY, +10% QoQ); non-GAAP GM 47% (+480bps YoY); non-GAAP EPS $4.10 (+115% YoY); FCF $953M, the highest in more than a decade; net leverage 0.7x; Fitch upgraded to investment grade. Exabytes 199 EB (+39% YoY) on flat units. Mozaic 4 began shipping; 75% of large cloud customers on Mozaic. Nearline almost fully allocated through CY2027; top-3 CSP RPO ~$1.1T. Annual revenue growth target raised to 'at least 20%.' Q4 guide: rev $3.45B, EPS $5.00.
JPM/Samik: ~90% sequential incremental gross margin, STX guiding opex ~$300M/qtr (operating leverage) and 'no need to give back price on generation changes' in a constrained market.

events.src: Morgan Stanley · Erik Woodring ('HDDs: The Next Leg Higher')
events.text: Nearline pricing escalators + HAMR ramp; Seagate the front-runner in HAMR (MS top pick). Vendors targeting ~$25/TB in CY27 and ~$30 in CY28 vs ~$14.50/TB today.

Seagate top pick in HDDs; 'raised numbers materially, again' on Asia checks. STX CY27 EPS = $52 (base), $66 (bull); 'if we took our checks as fact... more than $70 in CY27, more than $100 in CY28' → sub-10x in CY28 bull. Idiosyncratic edge: Google's 'sweetheart' HAMR contract should reprice higher from June to Sept-26, and STX ramps 40TB HAMR aggressively in 2H CY26 vs WDC only in H1 CY27.
GS desk 'firmly WDC > STX,' with WDC +48% in June vs STX 'only' +27%.

[AM, PRE-PRINT — 8am ET, ahead of the 7/28 AMC release.] Live HDD preview from the published 07-27 note's author, on the morning of the STX print (nothing superseded). The call: "I think we are going to get a pricing-driven beat and raise this quarter… [but] we've tried to kind of keep expectations in check because, at least in my conversations with investors, I felt like expectations have run a little bit rampant." The dispersion, quantified: the company is implying ~3-4% SEQUENTIAL price growth for the June quarter while "some of the higher end of bulls" sit at 8, 10, 12, 14% sequential. Where the upside actually comes from is uncontracted volume — from an Asia trip last month, "everyone that is not on an HDD contract is seeing significant price hikes. We're talking 30, 40 and in some cases 50%," with the sizing caveat kept ("a smaller part of both Seagate and WD's business. Nevertheless, it should have a decent impact this quarter"). He restates the HDD-is-not-memory separation verbally: ~50% gross margins with 70-80% incremental, "nowhere close to peak," revenue growth accelerating over the next five quarters, and no new capacity or supply visible "one, two, three years" out in a 3-player structure with no Chinese competitors. Host Sean adds a human-capital barrier to new supply, net-new: "anybody below 40 years old has no idea how to make hard disk drives anymore. These companies are sending engineers to universities to teach how to make these things." Cross-name framing for WDC: "I don't expect a lot of differentiation between the two of them when it comes to what they report or how they guide. Should be a nice beat and raise and the question is just how much pricing do we get this quarter?"
